title: Dependent profile resampling and observation inference

items.title: Affine normalization isometry for profile coordinates
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. For $a\in\mathbb R$ and $\ell>0$, let $I=(a,a+\ell)$, with Lebesgue measure, and let $H_I=L^2(I;\mathbb R)$ and $H_0=L^2((0,1);\mathbb R)$, both formed from measurable functions modulo equality almost everywhere. The map

$$U_{a,\ell}:H_I\to H_0,\qquad U_{a,\ell}[q]=[\xi\mapsto\sqrt{\ell}\,q(a+\ell\xi)]$$

is a well-defined linear isometric bijection. Its inverse is

$$V_{a,\ell}:H_0\to H_I,\qquad V_{a,\ell}[g]=[z\mapsto\ell^{-1/2}g((z-a)/\ell)].$$

references.title: Ohio State University, Math 6212 Real Analysis II, Theorem 137 (Change of variables) and proof, pp. 49–51

items.title: Profile-to-Hilbert bootstrap interface
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,\lambda;\mathbb R)$ be the real Hilbert space of almost-everywhere classes of square-integrable real profiles, with $\langle u,v\rangle_H=\int_0^1u(\xi)v(\xi)\,d\xi$, where $\mathcal B$ is generated by intervals with rational endpoints and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure restricted to $\mathcal B$. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ and $(S,\mathcal S,\nu)$ be probability spaces, let $(\delta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be independent identically distributed measurable $S$-valued random elements on $\Omega$ with law $\nu$, and let $f:S^{\mathbb N_0}\to H$ be measurable from the product sigma-algebra $\mathcal S^{\otimes\mathbb N_0}$ to the Borel sigma-algebra of $H$. The associated causal profile process is $X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\ldots)$. Assume $X_0$ is Bochner integrable and has Bochner mean $\mathbb E_BX_0:=\int_\Omega X_0(\omega)\,d\mathbb P(\omega)=0$, with $\mathbb E\|X_0\|_H^2<\infty$. Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice and take an independent product extension carrying the countable replacement-innovation family.

For every $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\ge1$, and $k\le t-m$, let $\delta'_{t,m,k}$ have law $\nu$, with all these copies mutually independent and independent of the original innovations. Set

$$X_{t,m}=f(\delta_t,\ldots,\delta_{t-m+1},\delta'_{t,m,t-m},\delta'_{t,m,t-m-1},\ldots),\qquad \delta_m=\bigl(\mathbb E\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_H^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

The profile process is $L^2$-$m$-approximable when $\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\delta_m<\infty$. For data $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in H$, $n\ge1$, and an integer block length $1\le b\le n$, moving-block resampling independently draws starts uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,n-b+1\}$, concatenates the corresponding ordered length-$b$ blocks, and truncates the last block to obtain exactly $n$ resampled elements $X_1^*,\ldots,X_n^*$. Define $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^*$, and let $\mathbb E^*$ denote expectation over these draws with the observations fixed. For any bounded real-linear functional $L:H\to\mathbb R$, let $\|L\|=\sup_{\|u\|_H\le1}|L(u)|$; the centered resampled scalar profile summary is $\sqrt n\,L(\bar X_n^*-\mathbb E^*\bar X_n^*)$. This definition specifies the data space and resampling law; it does not assert asymptotic validity.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving Block and Tapered Block Bootstrap for Functional Time Series with an Application to the K-Sample Mean Problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), §§2.1–2.2
L. Horváth, P. Kokoszka, and R. Reeder, Estimation of the Mean of Functional Time Series and a Two-Sample Problem, JRSS B 75 (2013), §1.1 and §2
A. DasGupta, Asymptotic Theory of Statistics and Probability, Chapter 29 §29.18, pp. 478–480

items.title: Bounded profile functional conditional CLT
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,\lambda;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathcal B$ is generated by intervals with rational endpoints and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure restricted to $\mathcal B$. Let $(S,\mathcal S,\nu)$ be a probability space, let $(\delta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be independent identically distributed $S$-valued innovations with law $\nu$, and let $f:S^{\mathbb N_0}\to H$ be measurable from the product sigma-algebra to the Borel sigma-algebra of $H$. Set $X_t=f(\delta_t,\delta_{t-1},\ldots)$ and assume its $H$-valued expectation is zero and $\mathbb E\|X_0\|_H^2<\infty$. For each $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\ge1$, and $k\le t-m$, let $\delta'_{t,m,k}$ have law $\nu$, with these copies mutually independent and independent of the original innovations, and set $X_{t,m}=f(\delta_t,\ldots,\delta_{t-m+1},\delta'_{t,m,t-m},\delta'_{t,m,t-m-1},\ldots)$. Assume $\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\delta_m<\infty$, where $\delta_m=(\mathbb E\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_H^2)^{1/2}$. For each $n\ge1$, let the integer block length $b_n$ satisfy $b_n\to\infty$ and $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$; for all sufficiently large $n$, apply moving-block resampling with block length $b_n$ to $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, truncating the last block to exactly $n$ elements. Write $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^nX_j^*$, and let $\mathbb E^*$ and $\operatorname{Cov}^*$ be expectation and covariance over resampling with the observations fixed. Let $G$ be the centered $H$-valued Gaussian limit with covariance operator $\Gamma$ supplied by the Hilbert-valued sample-mean CLT for this process. For any bounded real-linear $L:H\to\mathbb R$, set $\|L\|=\sup_{\|u\|_H\le1}|L(u)|$, let $h_L\in H$ be the unique vector satisfying $L(u)=\langle u,h_L\rangle_H$ for every $u\in H$, and define $L^*r=rh_L$. Identify the scalar operator $L\Gamma L^*:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with its value at $1$. Then
$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(\sqrt n\,L(\bar X_n^*-\mathbb E^*\bar X_n^*)\right)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(LG)\quad\text{in probability},$$
and, with $C_n=n\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)$,
$$\left|\operatorname{Var}^*\!\left(\sqrt n\,L(\bar X_n^*-\mathbb E^*\bar X_n^*)\right)-L\Gamma L^*\right|\le\|L\|^2\|C_n-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\longrightarrow0\quad\text{in probability}.$$
Here $L\Gamma L^*$ is the variance of the limiting scalar Gaussian. This conclusion concerns bounded linear profile observations under the stated Bernoulli-shift and block-length hypotheses; it makes no claim for nonlinear statistics or for finite-replicate quantile accuracy.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving Block and Tapered Block Bootstrap for Functional Time Series with an Application to the K-Sample Mean Problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), §2.2, Theorem 2.1, and §5
L. Horváth, P. Kokoszka, and R. Reeder, Estimation of the Mean of Functional Time Series and a Two-Sample Problem, JRSS B 75 (2013), Theorem 1 and Appendix A.1
A. DasGupta, Asymptotic Theory of Statistics and Probability, Chapter 29 §29.18, pp. 478–480

items.title: Scalar series as a constant Hilbert profile
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\epsilon_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be independent identically distributed real-valued innovations, and let $g:\mathbb R^{\mathbb N_0}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable from the product Borel sigma-algebra. Set $Y_t=g(\epsilon_t,\epsilon_{t-1},\ldots)$ and assume $\mathbb E Y_0=0$, $\mathbb E|Y_0|^2<\infty$. For each $t\in\mathbb Z$, $m\ge1$, and $k\le t-m$, let $\epsilon'_{t,m,k}$ have the same law as $\epsilon_0$, with these copies mutually independent and independent of the original innovations, and form $Y_{t,m}$ by replacing the innovations with indices $k\le t-m$ by these copies. Assume $\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}(\mathbb E|Y_0-Y_{0,m}|^2)^{1/2}<\infty$. Define $H=L^2([0,1],\mathcal B,\lambda;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathcal B$ is Borel and $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure, $X_t(\xi)=Y_t$ for almost every $\xi\in[0,1]$, and $L(v)=\int_0^1v(\xi)\,d\xi$. For each $n\ge1$, let integer block lengths $b_n\to\infty$ satisfy $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$. This constant-profile construction satisfies the centered causal $L^2$-$m$-approximability assumptions of the bounded profile-functional bootstrap proposition, and $L(X_t)=Y_t$.
